findings.issue: The dependency graph has a cycle, T1 -> T3 -> T2 -> T1, so none of T1-T3 can start, and T4 and T5 are blocked transitively. The migration (T1) has no valid reason to wait for the derived snapshot (T3).
findings.evidence: T1 after=[T3]; T3 after=[T2]; T2 after=[T1]. Requirement: 'All plan dependencies must be acyclic.' Baseline: 'Snapshot T3 is not a deployment prerequisite: it is derived repository metadata.'
findings.failure_scenario: A dependency-aware executor deadlocks or rejects the plan with nothing runnable. An executor that ignores the cycle runs the tasks in arbitrary order, and the results cannot be trusted.
findings.fix: Remove T3 from T1's after (T1 after=[]). The snapshot derives from the migration, never the reverse. With the T4 fix below, the DAG is T1 -> T2 -> {T3,T4} -> T5.

findings.issue: T2 and T4 both write packages/contracts/order.ts with no dependency path between them (both depend only on T1) and no merge owner. The shared 'order-contract' label does not serialize them. T4 also hand-patches a file that T2 describes as generated, so producer and consumer are not guaranteed to compile against one final definition.
findings.evidence: T2 writes=[apps/api/order-dto.ts,packages/contracts/order.ts], after=[T1]; T4 writes=[apps/web/order-client.ts,packages/contracts/order.ts], after=[T1]; both resources=[order-contract]; 'No merge owner exists.' Requirement: 'Two tasks that modify the same file must have an explicit dependency path or a named merge owner; resource labels alone do not lock tasks.' Baseline: generated contract files are checked in and both sides must compile against the same final definition.
findings.failure_scenario: T2 and T4 run in parallel after T1. One edit overwrites the other, or both add delivery_note and produce a merge conflict, duplicate declaration or divergent type (optional vs nullable). The API or client then compiles against a different contract, and the next regeneration silently drops T4's hand patch. Per-task rollback to the previous commit also cannot isolate the shared file.
findings.fix: Make T2 the only writer of packages/contracts/order.ts and remove that path from T4's writes. Set T4 after=[T2] so the client serializer consumes the final generated contract. Alternatively, name one explicit merge owner for the file and order T4 after it.

findings.issue: The verification command chains the checks with &&, so a failing lint stops typecheck and unit tests from running and leaves no exit status for them. This contradicts the requirement and T5's own acceptance criterion.
findings.evidence: command='npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test:unit'; acceptance='record the exit status of all three checks, including if lint fails'. Requirement: 'Execute lint, typecheck and unit tests even if an earlier command fails, recording an exit status for each.'
findings.failure_scenario: Lint exits non-zero and typecheck and test:unit never run. docs/run.md holds at most one status, T5 cannot meet acceptance, and type errors, test regressions or contract mismatches go undetected.
findings.fix: Run the three checks unconditionally, for example with a small bash script that runs each, captures its own exit code, writes all three codes to docs/run.md, and exits non-zero if any failed. Do not use &&.

uncertainties: The plan does not state whether 'npm run typecheck' compiles apps/api, apps/web and packages/contracts together. If it does not, no step verifies that producer and consumer compile against the same final contract.
